AboutIn.description:
What the screen showed when the person tapped "talk about this" (Guy, 13 Nov 2026): an insight, the question its
reading asked, or a follow-up. The text is what the app showed them, from their own data.
AboutIn.title: AboutIn

ActivityDetailsOut.description: What the health app recorded during one activity (Guy, 14 Nov 2026): only what exists, nothing estimated.
ActivityDetailsOut.title: ActivityDetailsOut

AnalyzeIn.description:
`also`: a second photo of the same meal, analysed together with this one. `note`: what the person wrote about the
photo before analysis, optional (Guy, 15 Nov 2026).
AnalyzeIn.title: AnalyzeIn

BirthIn.description: The date of birth as typed in onboarding (PM-248); only the day the person turns 18 is kept, if still ahead.
BirthIn.title: BirthIn

BodyDetailsOut.description: What is behind each "Body today" tile (Itay, 15 Nov 2026): today by hour, the last week by day, last night's stages.
BodyDetailsOut.title: BodyDetailsOut

BreakIn.description:
Turned on until it is turned off, or until a time (for an hour, until the morning, a chosen time); from now or
from a later time (`start`, PM-404).
BreakIn.title: BreakIn

BreakScheduleIO.description: The daily quiet schedule (PM-341): from and to as hh:mm on the person's clock, days 0 = Sunday to 6 = Saturday.
BreakScheduleIO.title: BreakScheduleIO

ChildActivityOut.description: The child's app activity for their parent (PM-444): counts, days and a time only, never content or values.
ChildActivityOut.title: ChildActivityOut

ClientErrorIn.description: A render error the app caught and survived (13 Nov 2026, the companion character crash). Code facts only.
ClientErrorIn.title: ClientErrorIn

ClinicReportIn.description: DAP-10: the period, the report's language (its own, not the app's), and what the person adds for this visit.
ClinicReportIn.title: ClinicReportIn

DeviceRatiosOut.description:
Carb ratio by time and correction factor as set on the connected pump (Tandem, 13 Nov 2026). While set, the
typed ones are kept as they were and cannot be edited in Stedio (G-48). Shown only; never used to suggest a dose.
DeviceRatiosOut.title: DeviceRatiosOut

EquipmentOut.description: The equipment rows at the bottom of Overview (Duet z21): only what a device or the person already said.
EquipmentOut.title: EquipmentOut

FoodNoteIn.description: What the person ate with this meal entry, in their words; empty or null removes it.
FoodNoteIn.title: FoodNoteIn

GlucosePatch.description: An edit makes a new revision; the previous values are kept.
GlucosePatch.title: GlucosePatch

GoalsIn.description: "What would you like us to help with?" and "What is hardest for you day to day?" (goals.py lists the values).
GoalsIn.title: GoalsIn

HabitData.description: A habit the person keeps track of (no sensor needed): done or not, with an optional amount in its own unit.
HabitData.title: HabitData

InterpretationOut.description: The model's reading of one insight (interpret.py): what the records show, possibilities, and what is missing.
InterpretationOut.title: InterpretationOut

InviteIn.description: An invite. Since DAP-19 the owner says what is shared and confirms the consent screen; `consent` must be true.
InviteIn.title: InviteIn

InvitePreviewOut.description: What an invite link shows before accepting: whose data and which parts. Nothing else about the owner.
InvitePreviewOut.title: InvitePreviewOut

LabData.description:
A lab or clinic result the person entered (13 Nov 2026), with the date it was taken and where it came from. Stored as
entered; Stedio does not grade it against a range.
LabData.title: LabData

LinesOut.description: The app's lines the phone hands the model, kept here with the rest of the companion's words.

dose.default: The app does not give insulin doses. Say so briefly and suggest the person follows their care team's plan.
dose.title: Dose

goodbye.default: The person is ending the call. Say one short, warm goodbye in their language and nothing more: no question and no new topic. The app then ends the call.
goodbye.title: Goodbye

stop.default: Stop speaking now and wait for the person to finish.
stop.title: Stop

unavailable.default: The app could not answer just now. Say so briefly and ask the person to try again in a moment.
unavailable.title: Unavailable

unheard.default: The app did not catch the person's words. Ask them briefly to say it again.
unheard.title: Unheard

working.default: The app is still working on what the person just told you (for example estimating a meal). Tell them in a few words that you're on it. Don't guess the result.
working.title: Working

LinesOut.title: LinesOut

NicknameIn.description: The viewer's own name for the person they follow. Empty or null goes back to the person's own name.
NicknameIn.title: NicknameIn

OnboardingAnswers.description: The onboarding draft from the app (version 1). Free text stays as typed; extra keys are rejected.
OnboardingAnswers.title: OnboardingAnswers

PartIn.description: A three-hour part of the day as the card shows it, in ms since 1970.
PartIn.title: PartIn

PendingOut.description: Someone new who follows the young person and waits for the parent's OK (PM-386).
PendingOut.title: PendingOut

PeriodBodyOut.description: Body data over a period (PM-397): each value is the mean of the days that have it, with how many days did.
PeriodBodyOut.title: PeriodBodyOut

Phone.description: What only the phone keeps, sent with a message for that answer only (never stored on the server).
Phone.title: Phone

Portion.description: One household measure of a food: the app unit it fills, its weight, and the database's Hebrew name for it.
Portion.title: Portion

PumpDayOut.description: One finished day as the pump's 30-day history reports it.
PumpDayOut.title: PumpDayOut

PumpStatusOut.description:
The pump's state at the last poll, as CareLink reported it. Every field is optional: older pumps or a pump out
of reach leave some out.
PumpStatusOut.title: PumpStatusOut

SameAsIn.description: The meal this entry is the same meal as, or null for "a separate meal".
SameAsIn.title: SameAsIn

ScopesIn.description: The owner changes what one person sees (permission settings), or who they are to them (PM-312), or both.
ScopesIn.title: ScopesIn

default.dose: The app does not give insulin doses. Say so briefly and suggest the person follows their care team's plan.
default.goodbye: The person is ending the call. Say one short, warm goodbye in their language and nothing more: no question and no new topic. The app then ends the call.
default.stop: Stop speaking now and wait for the person to finish.
default.unavailable: The app could not answer just now. Say so briefly and ask the person to try again in a moment.
default.unheard: The app did not catch the person's words. Ask them briefly to say it again.
default.working: The app is still working on what the person just told you (for example estimating a meal). Tell them in a few words that you're on it. Don't guess the result.

TandemPumpOut.description: What Tandem Source says about the pump, shown as set on the pump (read-only in Stedio, G-48).
TandemPumpOut.title: TandemPumpOut

TodayOut.description: Today so far from the health store (G-72): walking, heart rate, last night's sleep against the person's usual.
TodayOut.title: TodayOut

UpdatingOut.description: The sensor updating (PM-320): the pump says so and no reading has come since `since`. No reading is current.
UpdatingOut.title: UpdatingOut

UsualMealIn.description:
The foods as a saved meal stores them, for the whole served amount. A usual meal is the person's own, so it keeps
no estimate range or confidence: the app logs it again with its values as they were saved. `photo_id`: the meal's
first photo, when it had one (PM-425).
UsualMealIn.title: UsualMealIn

UsualMealPatch.description: PM-425: a new photo for the favorite (it replaces the one before), or that its photo was suggested.
UsualMealPatch.title: UsualMealPatch

UsualOut.description: One type's routine (G-67): middle of the last full days, weekdays and weekend, the busiest part of the day.
UsualOut.title: UsualOut

ViewerOut.description: A share as its owner sees it: who can see their data, or an invite not used yet.
ViewerOut.title: ViewerOut

ViewerRemindersOut.description:
The viewer's own set and sensor reminders about the person they follow (PM-422), and what can be chosen: the
sensor types the person's device services can tell the end of, and the set times for the person's set type.
ViewerRemindersOut.title: ViewerRemindersOut

ViewingOut.description: A share as the viewer sees it: whose data they can see, and which parts.
ViewingOut.title: ViewingOut

WarmupOut.description:
A new sensor warming up (G-80): no reading until `ready_at`, the maker's warm-up length after `started_at`.
From CareLink the pump itself says it is warming up; after `ready_at` it is still warming up ("any moment").
WarmupOut.title: WarmupOut

WhyOut.description: "Why am I seeing this?" for one insight: what it rests on and which of the person's goals it speaks to.
WhyOut.title: WhyOut

WordsIn.description: The card's words in the app's language: range labels, "not live · {t}" and "not current".
WordsIn.title: WordsIn

WorkoutsOut.description: Workouts and logged activity of the last weeks: how many, the person's own kinds, when, a middle length.
WorkoutsOut.title: WorkoutsOut

delete.description: Deletes the account and everything in it: rows go with the user (ON DELETE CASCADE), files with its folder.

get.description: Counts for the admin's analytics page (PM-446). See steady_api/admin_analytics.py.

post.description: Sends the update to everyone it reaches now. The page shows the reach and asks to confirm it first.

put.description:
Marks an existing account as a clinic team member of one clinic, with a role. The account must exist: the person
signs in once on the website first (Google, Apple or email).

delete.description: The account stays; it is no longer a clinic member and sees no patient.

schema.title: Response Admin Clinics Admin Clinics Get

delete.description: Only an empty clinic: its members must be moved or removed first. Its ended links go with it.

schema.title: Response List Requests Admin Demo Requests Get

post.description:
An admin invites someone by email (Guy, 18 Nov 2026): an approved request is made, or the person's open one is
used, and the personal link is emailed (shown once when no email can be sent).

delete.description: Deletes the request and its details (its sessions go with it).

post.description: Declined quietly: nothing is emailed.
The link stops working and its open demo sessions end.
A link for the team's own demos and scenario tests (Guy: also a tool to test scenarios). Not emailed.
Makes a Jira issue in the Support project from what the admin wrote. Once per request.

delete.description:
Deletes another account and everything in it, as the person's own "Delete account" does. Never the admin's own
account or another admin's, and only when the typed email matches the account's.

post.description: Takes an account off the waitlist (Guy, 12 Nov 2026) and emails it. Approving twice changes nothing.

Emails the person a reset code, as their own "Forgot password" does, saying support started it (PM-448). The admin
never sees or sets a password; the current one keeps working until the person sets a new one with the code.

409.description: no_password (signs in with Google or Apple only) or too_soon

post.description: Logs a caught app error for debugging: where, the message and the top frame, without the account or any values.

get.description: Public: it says only which build number is newest and where to install it.

post.description:
A second session for an admin, for the website's admin pages (PM-429). The website's "Sign in" opens the app,
whose sign-in is its own; an admin who signs in there is taken to the admin pages, which keep their session in
memory only, without signing in again. A new family, so signing out of either one leaves the other as it is.
Sign in or sign up with Apple (iPhone app), linked the same way as Google.

put.description:
PM-248: the date of birth from onboarding, so the server knows whether a parent must follow before anything else.
Under /auth/ so it answers while no parent follows yet. Only the day the person turns 18 is kept, if still ahead.

post.description:
Sign in or sign up with Google. The account is found by its Google id, else by the Google-verified email (an
account made with email and password is linked then), else made new without a password.

get.description: Where the person's own iPhone stands. An open link is checked with Expo first, so a phone just added shows.

post.description: The person's registration link: the open one they already have, or a new one. One link per account.

get.description:
Public (PM-353): whether testers can add their iPhone themselves (the Expo token is set). The guide asks for
sign-in only when this is true, so nobody signs in only to learn that it is not switched on.
Which ways to make an account are open, so the app and the website show only those.

post.description:
AUTH-04 (Guy, 14 Nov 2026): a 6-digit code by email to set a new password. The answer is the same whether or not an
account has this address, so it never tells who has one; at most one mail a minute per account. Without a mail
sender it says so (503) instead of pretending a mail went out.

schema.title: Response Forgot Password Auth Password Forgot Post

post.description: The emailed code and a new password: the password is set, every other session ends, and this one signs in.

put.description: DAP-7: who the person is here for. Under /auth/ so an account on the waitlist can answer it too.

post.description: Sends a new code to the signed-in account's email (not more than once a minute).

delete.description: The person stops sharing with a clinic (or withdraws from a request). Takes effect on the clinic's next request.

put.description: The person sends their questions for the visit to this clinic. Kept until 7 days after the visit.

delete.description: A team member withdraws a request or stops seeing a person. The person's summaries for this clinic go too.

schema.title: Response Clinic Patients Clinic Patients Get
Response Clinic Series Clinic Patients  Link Id  Series  Name  Get
Response Clinic Summary Page Clinic Patients  Link Id  Summary Get

post.description:
The person read and agreed to these versions. Refused as a whole when any of them is no longer the one in force,
so a record always names the text the person saw. Recorded once per version (append-only history). The AI consent
can be withdrawn with `POST /consent/ai/off` and given again here; the others end by deleting the account.

409.description: version_changed: a newer version came out; ask again

post.description:
The person agreed to send their data to the external AI engine, from an app build of PM-149. Those builds show the
first text of the consent and send no version, so the record is for that text only: once the consent has a newer
text, this does not open the AI engine, and the person is asked again by a newer app (`/consent/accept`).

The person turned the AI features off in Settings > Privacy (PM-177): a withdrawal record, so from now on nothing
about them is sent to the external AI engine (every AI route and the background readings check `ai_consent`), and
the AI consent is not asked for again. Turning it on again is `POST /consent/accept` with the current AI version.
What the AI engine already wrote (conversations, insight readings) stays until the person deletes it.

The consents a person gave on the onboarding consent step, recorded before the profile is saved (PM-245): the app
sends them before a data connection (CareLink, Dexcom, Libre, Tandem, the phone's health store) starts during
onboarding, so no device data arrives without a consent record. The same records and rules as the profile save
(`record_consents`), which later finds them already there and adds nothing. Refused without the service consent and
the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy, which onboarding requires before this point.
The companion opens about the item the person was looking at, already knowing it, with a short first line.

get.description: A conversation's messages, oldest first. Without an id: the current one, or none after a quiet gap.

post.description: What the person did with a proposal card: saved (or waiting to sync) through the records API, or dismissed.

Save on a log card (meal, activity, insulin, note): the server writes the record the card shows. A retry returns
the saved card; a card that was dismissed or replaced by a newer one is not saved.

get.description:
The companion's speech bubbles on the main screen: a greeting and follow-ups from the person's own recent
conversations and logs. Answers at once with what is kept; stale follow-ups are written again after the answer.

Past conversations for the history sheet: a short title the AI engine wrote (the first message until then), the
companion's last reply as one line, and when. Missing titles are written in the background (PM-220).

delete.description:
The person deletes a conversation from the list (Guy, 18 Nov 2026, PM-220): its messages, their recall vectors,
tool logs and quality reviews go with it (cascade). What they asked the companion to remember stays in Memories,
where it is deleted on its own. The main screen's follow-up bubbles are written again, so none comes from it.

post.description:
A past conversation opened from the list goes on (PM-220): it becomes the current one, so voice and "talk about
this" continue it too. The app calls this when the person starts talking in it, not when they only read it.

The clinic portal in the demo (PM-275): the demo clinician's session, with the demo people linked to the demo
clinic. Same personal link as the app demo; the clinic side stays read-only for this account.

schema.title: Response Request Demo Demo Requests Post

post.description: A demo session with the scenario's shared demo account, for a valid personal link. No username or password.

delete.description: Forgets the CareLink sign-in. With remove_readings, the readings that came from CareLink are deleted too.

put.description: Signs in to CareLink now. Only a sign-in that worked is kept; a refused one is answered and forgotten.

post.description: Starts a sign-in on CareLink's own page, for when CareLink asks for more than the password (G-29).
Finishes a sign-in made on CareLink's page with the address CareLink returned, and fetches the readings.

get.description: The person's device connections and whether each still brings data, for the "connection lost" banner.

delete.description: Forgets the sign-in. With remove_readings, the readings that came from this source are deleted too.

put.description: Signs in now. Only a sign-in that worked is kept; a refused one is answered and forgotten.

get.description:
The set change and the sensor's time left, read only. A follower may read it with the glucose (PM-422, Guy 22 Nov
2026: someone viewing another person's data sees the set and sensor rows too); only these two values, the device
connection itself stays private.
The pump's alerts and messages in a period, for the journal (Guy, 12 Nov 2026), oldest first.

schema.title: Response Device Events Devices Events Get

delete.description: Forgets the sign-in. With remove_readings, the readings that came from this source are deleted too.

put.description: Signs in now. Only a sign-in that worked is kept; a refused one is answered and forgotten.

get.description:
Pump modes that overlap a period (Guy, 16 Nov 2026: Sport mode), oldest first, so the journal can show each
mode and badge the readings and insulin inside it.

schema.title: Response Device Modes Devices Modes Get

put.description: A token belongs to one account at a time: signing in elsewhere on the same phone moves it.

post.description:
"I changed my set" (Guy, 14 Nov 2026): CareLink reports a set change only in its daily history, hours later, so the
person can say it now. Kept like a pump's set change (one a day), which ends the "set past its days" card.

delete.description: Forgets the sign-in. With remove_readings, the readings that came from this source are deleted too.

put.description: Signs in now. Only a sign-in that worked is kept; a refused one is answered and forgotten.

get.description:
Whether a new sensor is warming up, or the sensor is updating (PM-320), now, from the connected device services
(read only). A follower may read it with the glucose (deps.SCOPE_PATHS): it is why no current reading is shown.

delete.description: Turning the weather off forgets the kept state and the daily summary.

post.description: Coordinates are rounded and used once for the lookup; only the derived state and a daily summary are kept.

delete.description:
Deletes a report or export the person made, before its 7 days are up (Guy, 21 Nov 2026, PM-349: "a report I made,
let me delete it"): the sealed file and its row. One already gone (expired or deleted) is a 404.

get.description: Follow-ups due in [since, until), plus any still waiting from before `since` (overdue and not closed).

schema.title: Response List Follow Ups Follow Ups Get

put.description:
Take a break (PM-257, Guy 18 Nov 2026): until turned off or until the time given, the app is one screen with the
latest reading and no push goes out but the out-of-range look-back the person turned on. Check-ins wait as in a
pause; the app starts none.
The daily quiet schedule (PM-341): quiet mode turns on and off by itself on the chosen days.

Fewer nudges (burnout mode, DAP-18, 16 Nov 2026): for a while, or until turned off, the app starts at most one
check-in a day, pushes no insights, wins or compliments, and the companion keeps it short. Reminders the person set
and their devices' alerts are unchanged.

post.description: The offer was turned down: it stays away for a month.

put.description:
Pause check-ins (RTN-05, 14 Nov 2026): for an hour, the rest of the day, three days or until turned back on.
Check-ins due meanwhile are withdrawn (a daily one moves to its first day after). Reminders the person set
themselves still arrive.

delete.description: Withdraws this follow-up, or with `series` every open occurrence of a daily one.

post.description: The phone scheduled a local notification for this due time.
"Not today" from the notification (RTN-07): a daily one moves to tomorrow, a one-off is dismissed.
A finished game's points. Every point becomes a coin (no daily limit, Guy 23 Nov 2026).

delete.description:
Disconnecting with "Remove imported readings" (SET-05): every reading that came from the phone's health store is
soft deleted. Readings the person entered themselves are not touched.

post.description:
Readings read from Apple Health or Health Connect, in batches. Each sample is stored once (its store id is the
idempotency key), labelled with the store as its source, and never overwrites what the person entered or corrected.
Values outside the entry limits (G-06) are skipped, not changed.

delete.description: Soft delete: gone from the journal and summaries; kept until account deletion. A device's reading can't be (PM-362).

409.description: source_read_only: the reading came from a device
source_read_only: the reading came from a device

schema.title: Response Revisions Glucose  Record Id  Revisions Get

get.description:
Steps and active energy as a routine, with the person's best day (G-67). Empty values until there are enough days.
kinds=2 adds exercise minutes, stood hours and the workouts summary (G-69), for app code that knows them.

The nights that overlap [since, until), as "Body today" builds them (one source per night, the one that saw most of
it), for the sleep icons under the glucose graph (Guy, 18 Nov 2026, PM-244). Only what the health store recorded.

schema.title: Response List Nights Health Data Nights Get

get.description: The body over the local days `from`..`to`, both included (Guy, 21 Nov 2026, PM-397: the Overview's period).

schema.title: Response List Samples Health Data Samples Get

get.description:
The body over the `hours` hours up to `until` (default now; an earlier 24 hours with the Overview's arrows), rolling
(Guy, 23 Nov 2026, PM-420: the Overview's 24h filter). `until` is never after now nor more than 92 days back.
`shown=true`: the client lists these insights on screen now, so each listing is kept as learning data.
The first days (RTN-01): which day, entries per day, first impressions of the routine, and what is not known yet.
RTN-02: the first-days summary. Counts and the meal times seen; impressions the person can confirm or reject.

post.description: Keep the extra check-ins a few more days: getting to know the person goes on for EXTEND_DAYS more days, once.

put.description: The person's answer on an impression ("Sounds right" / "Not really"); null clears it.

post.description: A card under the companion that is not an insight, marked as read: left out of the main screen on every device.

get.description:
Each hour of the day over the last 14 days (for the lock-screen widget, G-40): how many days had readings then and
how many of those days were above, below or in the person's own range, by that day's middle value in the hour.
With span=3 the blocks are three hours long (00-03, 03-06, ...), for the lock-screen card's part of the day (G-41).
How far the order of insights has learned from the person (warming up, learning, checking, personal).

schema.title: Response Learning Status Insights Learning Get

get.description: The learning timeline, one entry per day since day 1: what was collected and what became known.

The mentor moment for the main screen now (PM-432): one card before a meal the person usually has, chosen from
their own past records, and one look back after it. Never for someone viewing the person's data.

schema.title: Response Get Moment Insights Moment Get

get.description: Recent insight updates (new, changed, follow-up, ended, corrected), newest first, whether pushed or not.

schema.title: Response List Updates Insights Updates Get

post.description: What the person did with an insight, kept apart from opening it and from what they said about it.
A personal reading of one current insight. Not for someone viewing a shared account (it would be kept as theirs).
Seen or read on a screen: kept on the server, so the app and the website show the same state.

get.description:
Every lab result the person saved, newest first, for the results table (PM-213). Lab results matter over years, so
unlike /records this has no 92-day window. A viewer with the journal shared sees them too (deps.VIEW_PATHS).

delete.description:
Deletes one test date's results, the whole report as listed in My test results (Guy, 21 Nov 2026, PM-348: swipe a
report away). Soft delete like a single record: gone from every screen and summary; the rows and their revisions stay
until account deletion.

get.description:
A packaged food by its barcode (PM-242), from Open Food Facts and then, for products it doesn't have, USDA
FoodData Central's branded foods (PM-336): carbs, fiber, protein and fat per 100 g as on the label, and the
label's serving when it has one. Only the barcode number leaves the server. 404 when no source has the product
with a carbohydrate value; the app then offers a photo or a search. 502 when none has it and a source failed.

A Hebrew query searches the Israeli food list (Ministry of Health, Tzameret; DAP-16) with typical portions. A Latin
query searches USDA FoodData Central as before, followed by up to five foods of the Israeli list by their English
names. The Israeli list is part of the server, so it answers when USDA is not configured or does not answer.

The photo of a saved meal, for its Journal card (Guy, 13 Nov 2026); gone once removed. Also for someone the person
shares their journal with, view only (PM-310): with X-View-As the user here is the person who shares (deps).
A favorite's own photo (PM-425) is shown to its owner only.

schema.title: Response List Usual Meal Usual Get

get.description:
Average glucose by 3-hour part of the day. With from/to: over that shown period (at most 92 days; the part after now
has no data yet, and "days" counts the whole period). Without: the last 7, 14, 30 or 90 local days, today included.

schema.title: Response Get Averages Metrics Averages Get

get.description: Weekly windows up to yesterday (local), the baseline, and whether a change held (see metrics.progress).

schema.title: Response Get Progress Metrics Progress Get

get.description: Data quality: each source's measured rhythm, duplicates and overlaps dropped, gaps and coverage per day.

schema.title: Response Get Quality Metrics Quality Get

get.description: The spread of glucose by time of day over [from, to) (default: the last 14 days), and whether there was enough.

schema.title: Response Get Typical Day Metrics Typical Day Get

get.description: The note for a subject (a local date, a week's Monday, a visit date), or the latest of that kind. None when none.

schema.title: Response Get Note Notes  Kind  Get

put.description: The person says the day's meals are all logged (or not). Only today and earlier.

schema.title: Response Mark Day Nutrition Days  Day  Put

get.description:
The last `days` local days up to today, or the local days `from`..`to` (both included, at most 92, not after
today) for the day by day list (Guy, 18 Nov 2026, PM-255).

The target range and carb ratios from a connected pump, also before any profile exists (PM-245): a pump connected
during onboarding shows its settings on the ratios step, which the profile save then keeps from the pump (G-48).
Changes to the profile answers, newest first (at most 100), optionally for one section ("food", "goals").

schema.title: Response Profile History Profile History Get

get.description:
Wins of the last 14 days, newest first (the daily check runs here too if it is due). `kinds=2`: the client knows
personal bests of steps and active energy (G-67); older app code doesn't get them.

post.description: Seen, or the celebration shown: once, anywhere. A second celebration of the same win is refused (409).

get.description: `kinds=2`: the client knows lab results and habits (13 Nov 2026); older app code gets only the kinds it knows.

delete.description:
Soft delete: gone from the journal and summaries; the row and its revisions stay until account deletion. A device's
entry can't be deleted (PM-362); it can be hidden.

409.description: source_read_only: the record came from a device
source_read_only: the record came from a device

put.description:
What the person ate, in their own words, on a meal entry (Guy, 16 Nov 2026: the pump records only the carbs that were
entered, so let the person write what they ate). Only the note changes: the carbs, time and source stay as the pump
recorded them, nothing is sent back to the device, and no revision is made (the note saves itself as it is typed).

Marks this meal entry as the same meal as another (G-47), or, with null, as a separate meal. The entry that points
is shown and counted with the other. Either side can be named: when the other one is a device's entry and this one
is not, the device's entry is the one that points.

post.description:
A clinic report (DAP-10) for the last `days` local days, made in the background like an export and kept as one for
EXPORT_DAYS. The person shares it themselves; nothing is sent from here.

get.description: The whole catalog. The check runs here too, so a new unlock shows as soon as the app asks.

post.description: Seen, or the celebration shown (which is also seen). Once, anywhere; unknown or locked ids are ignored.
The viewer enters the code. It works once, within 7 days, and not for one's own data.

get.description: An invite link opened by someone signed in: whose data and which parts, before they accept.

delete.description:
The owner removes a viewer or cancels an invite; the viewer stops viewing. Takes effect on the next request. The
viewer's conversations about the owner's data go too (DAP-19): consent withdrawn means nothing from it is kept.

patch.description: The owner changes what one person sees, an invite or an accepted share. Takes effect on the next request.

post.description: A parent's cheer (PM-300), or any follower's for an adult they follow (PM-304).

put.description: The viewer names the person they follow (PM-385). Only the viewer sees it; nothing of the owner's changes.

get.description: The viewer's own reminders about the person they follow (PM-422). Only the viewer reads or sets them.

put.description: Sets the viewer's own set and sensor reminders about the person they follow. Sent to the viewer only.

get.description: How the child used Stedio in their last 7 or 30 days, for the confirmed parent only (PM-444).

post.description:
The parent's OK for someone new who follows their child (PM-386), or a no: approved, the share opens; declined, it
ends as if the child had removed them (their conversations about the child go too).

get.description:
Whether a voice provider is configured, so the app can show the unavailable state before anyone talks. The
voice screen asks this when it opens, so the slow part of the companion's context is built now, ahead of a call.

post.description: Whether the companion's words so far read as a dose instruction; the phone then stops her at once.
What the call should know about glucose now, polled by the phone during a call; marks a check-in as raised.
Keeps a turn the companion answered by herself in the conversation, like text (checked by the dose rule).
Answers one delegation: the text companion with its tools, on what the person just said.

get.description: A stored companion reply, spoken. A withheld reply has no text and is not spoken.
One fixed sample sentence in a chosen voice and language, with the mentor's fixed name. Not a speech service.

put.description:
Which proactive messages stay in the app instead of WhatsApp (the rest go to WhatsApp). After the person asked on
WhatsApp to stop them (PM-365), turning any kind on here restarts WhatsApp updates for the kinds left on.

delete.description:
Unlinks the number: the WhatsApp consent is withdrawn, the number deleted, and one goodbye line sent if the free
window is still open.

post.description: The person agreed to the WhatsApp consent and asked to link: a new one-time code inside a wa.me link.
